protocol.bootstrap: paired by seed, resampled with replacement, B=10000, 95% percentile interval
conditions: direct-additive (0->16:+dW, 1->17:+dW only, matches relay's purely-additive shape)

question: A2 found direct-contrastive beats relay, but contrastive also suppresses the competing output while relay does not -- confounding amplitude with discrimination margin. A3 adds direct-additive (matches relay's own bias shape: only adds to the correct output) and calibrates every condition against the SAME seed range (A2 used disjoint ranges for relay vs direct), then measures both output channels under both cues to show the match, not assert it.

calibration.note: hzTable shows output16/output17 under both cues for all four conditions at identical seed base -- direct-additive and relay should match on BOTH channels if the calibration and bias-shape fix worked; direct-contrastive should show a suppressed competing channel; original is the unbiased baseline.

limitations: Host CPU fixtures. Single calibration stimulus intensity (500Hz, 30ms). Spike-timing distributions, intensity sweep, window-duration sweep and per-decision compute cost (Sol's broader measurement list) are not covered here -- this file targets only the narrow additive-vs-relay comparison Sol asked for as the closing experiment of this series. A true recurrent (feedback) circuit on a state-holding task is explicitly out of scope here and remains open future work.
